answer: Each submission hangs on the vertex of a task receipt, and the echo is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a plain sentences, numbers cited inline register, it stays short. The design leans on receipt hashes checked against public logs before trust. The ripple of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
